To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
combined intraportal infusion with adrenergic antagonists and ACh augments net hepatalic glucose uptake in the conscious dog.

portal glucose infusion in the fasted dog augments hepatic glucose utilization, that this effect is mediated by a combination of acetylcholinesterase inhibition and adrenergically mediated vasoconstriction, and that portal glucose delivery in the dog is a useful model of the hepatic glucose metabolism in humans.
the infusion of ACh into the hepatic portal vein in the presence of somatostatin-induced basal hepatic sinusoidal insulin and glucagon concentrations augments NHGU in the conscious dog.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of net hepatic glucose output (NHGO) and uptake (NHGU) in the conscious dog.
the role of autonomic nerves in the regulation of hepatic glucose metabolism.
the role of portal glucose delivery in the regulation of hepatic glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ACh infusion in the presence of adrenergically blocked portal vein enhances the NHGU.
ACh and adrenergics have a role in the regulation of glucose metabolism in the liver.

the combined infusion of adrenergics and cholinergic blockers in the portal circulation increases NHGU in the presence of hyperglycemia-hypersinusoidal insulinemia-hyperglucagonemia in the conscious dog.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the net hepatic balance of glucose and lactate are both switched from output to uptake by portal glucose delivery in 42-h fasted dogs.
portal glucose delivery increases NHGU by increasing insulin-stimulated NHGU and decreasing glucagon-mediated hepatic glucose production.
the increase in NHU seen after portal glucose is mediated by a combination of the direct effect of glucose and the effect of glucose to alter nerve activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ACh is an important regulator of hepatic glucose metabolism.
the increase in NHUG is due to the increase in insulin sensitivity of the hepatocytes, and this is mediated by the parasympathetic nervous system.
the autonomic nervous system can be used therapeutically to augment glucose disposal.
